utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number: IT-01-42-PT, the Prosecutor versus Miodrag Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. May I have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, Susan L. Somers. To my right, Mr. Vladimir Tochilovsky; to my left, Mr. Massimo Scaliotti; and Ms. Susan Grogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Somers. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour, I am alone today representing Mr. Jokic. My name is Zarko Nikolic, and I am an attorney from Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Nikolic. Since this is the first time we meet in respect of the Jokic case, I'd like to introduce myself as well. My name is Alphonsus Orie, and I'm the Pre-Trial Judge in this case. The main purpose of a Status Conference is to find out whether the trial preparation, especially the communication between the parties, develops as it should develop. Might I perhaps first ask Mr. Nikolic whether the change of counsel caused any specific problems as far as disclosure and trial preparation is concerned. And more specifically, on whether the communication with former Defence counsel is going as it should go.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before I respond to this question, I would like to inform you that after the decision from the registrar that I was appointed as Defence for Mr. Jokic, in first contacts with him, I suggested and advised him to behave strictly in accordance with the decision of the Trial Chamber regarding his provisional release. So I believe that there will be no problems in this regard and that you will be regularly informed about his conduct. I have taken all the documents which have been presented to the accused, Mr. Jokic, and all the documents are in B/C/S. The English versions which were handed over to the previous Defence, I still have not received so far, even though I have attempted to make contact with them. So in that regard, I would like to tell you that on the 7th of March, after Mr. Jokic requested that I be his Defence, I did get in touch with the Prosecution, and we tried to get some kind of agreement on how we could resolve this problem. After I returned to Yugoslavia, even though I still haven't officially been informed, an e-mail has been sent to Mr. Jones in order for him to return all the documentation that he has in his possession. So far, we haven't had a response from him. This morning also we had a meeting with the OTP. I think it was quite a constructive meeting. I hope the other side will confirm this. And we agreed that perhaps one way to resolve this is to ask through the Registry that Mr. Jones return all the documents regarding this case, whether to the Prosecution, to the Registry, or directly to myself as the Defence attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So there are some problems as far as the transfer of disclosed documents is concerned. Of course, I'm quite glad that there is a -- that there is a positive communication between Defence and Prosecution in this respect. If the problem would not be solved on short notice, then if you would need the assistance of the Chamber or perhaps first the assistance of the Senior Legal Officer, but if necessary also the Chamber to give any orders to former Defence counsel, please let us know. Is there anything else at this moment you'd like to bring to our attention in respect of the case? I'll later ask you whether there are any other personal circumstances of Mr. Jokic which need attention, but as far as the case is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At present, there are no problems, Your Honour. We have experience from another case in view of the fact that Ms. Somers was also the prosecuting attorney there. So we today agreed for all outstanding questions, to resolve them in direct contact so that we wouldn't burden the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you understand that is always a message we gladly receive, that you are solving your problems, the parties, among each other themselves. But of course, if necessary, you can always address the Chamber. Ms. Somers, may I then ask you whether the Prosecution is of the same opinion, that there aren't any problems and apart from communication with former Defence counsel? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I do whole-heartedly confirm that. Mr. Nikolic and I have very good communication. And he did make me aware of the issue of non-receipt of the documents, and the Prosecution found itself in complete compliance with its 66(A)(i) obligations. And it is a concern to us, but particularly in light of this Chamber's protective order issued the 16th of January, where point 7 says, "If a member of the Strugar and Jokic Defence team withdraws, all material in his or her possession shall be returned to their lead Defence counsel," who is of course now this counsel. We have made it clear that we will assist Mr. Nikolic in any way possible to get, before his departure, the B/C/S -- all the B/C/S documents. It was my understanding from our productive meeting this morning that not all the B/C/S documents were in his possession, bits and pieces. And so we want to make sure that he has everything. He has also made a request for the English documentation. We've discussed it, and we believe will be able to accommodate in due course. The other aspects of pre-trial, the pre-trial process leading up to 65 ter obligations, we have discussed at length, including meeting to try to resolve -- to determine what can be admitted, what remains in dispute factually and legally. There are other matters that have to do with other provisions of the Rules that we have discussed. And again I think that there is nothing else that we could add. We are hopeful that he will be able to pick up quickly the other materials. In the alternative, I believe, if I'm correct, Mr. Nikolic said that he requested either that the materials be sent directly to him or sent to the Office of the Prosecutor. I would let the Chamber know we do not -- we've had no communication with Mr. Jones, and we have received nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your information, Ms. Somers. Mr. Nikolic, you already referred to the situation of provisional liberty Mr. Jokic is enjoying at this moment. Are there any personal aspects which you deem necessary to, or you deem it wise to, bring to the attend of the Trial -- Pre-Trial -- or the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, absolutely not at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I hope that the limited time we needed for this Status Conference will not disappoint you, but if the communication between the parties is developing well, not only in respect of disclosure obligations but also in order to find out what is in dispute, what is not in dispute, then of course that might save a lot of time later on. I think the Pre-Trial Judge can only be happy. So therefore, I would like to ask either party whether there's anything else we need to discuss at this very moment. I see nodding no four times.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much for your appearance. This concludes that Status Conference.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference was adjourned
